newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S STALS SAYS IMF DECISION POLITICAL - RADIO.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S STALS SAYS IMF DECISION POLITICAL - RADIO.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Thursday that a decision on whether the country should seek an International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan was a political decision.
He had given his views but the decision rested with government, SABC radio quoted him as saying in an off-air interview.
There have been growing calls for the authorities to seek IMF assistance to bolster reserves, as a back-up for the scrapping of exchange controls.

The continuation of exchange controls is frequently cited as a major facor destabilsing the rand. Critics say that as long as controls remain it is impossible to determine the correct value of the currency, which has tumbled to successive lows recently.
Under IMF rules, South Africa would be able to draw up to 100 percent of its IMF quota -- or some $2 billion -- for use as a standby or extended fund facility.
IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said earlier this month that the institution was prepared to support South Africa's reserves and provide funding, if asked.
